description: We are some folks who work with digital twins and are interested in the stories that data can communicate to us.
summary: The Panoptic Explorer is a web application that democratizes satellite imagery, particularly NISAR data, by providing an interface for a broad audience to explore how the stories of real-world events are written remote sensing data. The Panoptic Explorer can display a story for any significant event within view of the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar. It provides explorable views of satellite data projected on realistic terrain, and presents analysis using simple, transparent rules that have been cross-checked against multiple data sources. It also brings in additional context using open-source community and road network data. This platform is important because disasters often hide from optical satellites when the people directly affected need answers. Our open pipeline turns free NISAR data into stories that anyone can understand, and new events can be added to the library without changing the application.
details:
The Panoptic Explorer was developed along two parallel tracks:


1. Data ingestion and analysis pipeline

2. Web application for visualization and storytelling

The data ingestion pipeline was developed in python journals with data with pandas, plotly, numpy, shapely, and pyproj as the toolset. The journals search NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) for NISAR granules over a selected study area using the EarthData Login API. They use GCOV (radar backscatter), GUNW (interferometric coherence), SME2 (soil moisture), and Urgent Response products to determine how a region changes around the time of the selected event. They then build a structured story manifest for ingestion by the web application. The project as submitted tells five stories from 2026: the Gandak flood in India, a glacier collapse in Nepal, an oil spill off Oman, and two wildfires in Canada. More can be added easily using the established story manifest structure.

The web application uses React, DeckGL, and Three.js to build a responsive, intuitive visualization and exploration platform with 3D capabilities. The landing page introduces the project, and users are directed to a global map view with clearly highlighted case studies. Selecting the case studies displays NISAR data directly on the map, and allows the user to access the Case Study view. Each case study contains a guided short story built directly from the manifest generated by the python journals.
